hints: Suppose the answer contained two readings with a third reading between them that was left out. Could that happen?
It could not: anything between two chosen readings is at least as close to the target as the further of the two. So the answer is a contiguous run of length `k`.
Now there are only `n - k + 1` possible runs, each defined by its left end. Compare a run against the one starting one place later: which of the two boundary readings is further from the target?
That comparison is monotone, so binary search the left end over `0 .. n - k`, comparing `target - readings[mid]` against `readings[mid + k] - target`.
